title: Implicit Status-Based Update Convention
pattern: An object provides update/modifier methods that assume an implicit state machine invariant (e.g., can only be called when status is LOADING) but do not assert it.
why_bad: Developers can invoke modifier methods at incorrect times (e.g., after the object is committed/frozen), causing invalid state corruption or silent database synchronization anomalies.
detection: A modifier method updates fields of an object without verifying an internal state variable or calling an assertion guard.
counterexample: Asserting the state inside the method: `Assert.isTrue(state == LOADING);`.
fix: Enforce the status-based guard explicitly in the modifier: `fn update_name(&mut self, name: String) { assert_eq!(self.state, State::Loading); self.name = name; }`.
source: [The Addison-Wesley signature series] Martin Fowler - PEAA, p. 648 [648].
